findings.text: A globally visible helper reports a reusable delay calibration value for the current processor, returning zero when no reuse is allowed and otherwise returning a value learned on another processor.
A globally visible fault handler attempts to emulate a user instruction blocked by user mode instruction prevention, reporting whether the fault was handled.
A globally visible logging helper emits rate limited kernel messages for user mode prevention events together with task and register context.
Two alternative globally visible initializers prepare an unwind state from a task plus registers or a first frame pointer, selecting stack information and advancing to the requested starting frame.
A globally visible flag records whether the time stamp counter has been observed to reset asynchronously across processors.
Frequency selection capacity is sixteen entries, matching a four bit selector.
The MSR derived frequency reference base is one hundred thousand kilohertz.
A ratio record contains a multiplier part and a divider part used to derive a processor frequency from a platform frequency.

A frequency descriptor contains a flag for platform register use, a table of ratios sized by the selection capacity, a parallel table of fixed frequencies for cases without usable ratios, and a selector mask.

Two early low power descriptors do not use the platform register, use a three bit mask, and provide only fixed frequencies with sparse populated entries holding 99840 and 83200, with one variant additionally holding 133200.
One Silvermont tablet descriptor uses the platform register with a three bit mask and five fractional scalings clustered near unity.
One Airmont descriptor uses the platform register with a four bit mask and nine fractional scalings clustered near unity.
One Silvermont mobile descriptor uses the platform register with a three bit mask and only two effective scalings, unity and four thirds, with an empty first entry.
One Annalee descriptor uses the platform register with a four bit mask and four fractional scalings near unity.
One Lightning Mountain descriptor uses the platform register with a four bit mask but provides a uniform fixed frequency table where every entry holds 78000.
A terminated match table associates seven low power processor identities with their corresponding frequency descriptors.
Per processor adjustment state holds a boot time counter value, an adjusted value, a deadline for the next check expressed in timer ticks, and a flag recording whether a warning was issued.
Adjustment state exists per processor while a single global timer object drives periodic verification across online processors.
Periodic time stamp verification runs every six hundred seconds.

The periodic check verifies adjustment state and then migrates the timer to the next online processor, wrapping to the first when the end is reached, and it is not started when adjustment support is absent or the time source is already deemed reliable.

Cross processor synchronization uses paired start and stop counters plus a remaining attempts counter, together with records for the last observed counter value, the largest observed backward step, total steps and randomly ordered steps.
A global architecture specific spin lock in unlocked initial state serializes time stamp synchronization measurements.

Source side synchronization allows a single attempt without adjustment support and up to three attempts with it, passing when no backward step is seen, retrying when correction may help, and otherwise disabling the time source, with state reset before each retry and before releasing the peer.
A work handler marks the time stamp time source unstable after a failed synchronization check.

Two time stamp clock sources share the same read routine, sixty four bit mask, continuity and verification behavior, virtualization mode and lifecycle callbacks, while the later one carries rating 300 versus 299 for the early one and additionally advertises inline reads and coupled event support.

Calibration starts from an early low rated source, performs a delayed remeasurement against a platform reference, adopts the refined rate only when close to the initial estimate, then registers the full rated source and retires the early one, skipping refinement when the rate is already known from hardware identity.

Delay calibration may be reused from the boot processor when the counter is constant and stable, or from another online processor in the same core group when stable sharing across sockets is unavailable.
Known frequency paths warn when the remeasured rate deviates beyond about five hundred parts per million, while unknown paths adopt the new rate only within one percent.
Emulated descriptor bases are fixed constants near the top of canonical space, with the global table value at hex FFFFFFFFFFFE0000 and the interrupt table value at hex FFFFFFFFFFFF0000.
Emulated descriptor results use eight base bytes in sixty four bit mode, four base bytes otherwise, plus a two byte limit.
Five emulated instructions are numbered zero through four for global table store, interrupt table store, machine status word store, local table store and task register store.
Instruction numbers map to short names in order, log output carries a common short prefix, and error versus debug helpers share one underlying printer with distinct severity.
User mode prevention logging is rate limited to five messages every two minutes and includes task identity plus instruction and stack pointers.

An instruction classifier accepts only two byte opcodes beginning with fifteen followed by zero or one, distinguishes five cases by extension field, and rejects register forms that encode unrelated system or virtualization operations.

Emulation returns dummy table bases with zero limit for table stores, and returns fixed control, task or local table values for the other three cases, sizing register results by operand width and memory results to two bytes.
Local table emulation holds a read lock while testing whether a user local table exists, releasing it before producing the result.
When writing an emulated result to user memory fails, the fault is converted into a user write page fault signal with map error semantics rather than returning an error to the caller.

The top level fixup declines when prevention is disabled or decoding fails, otherwise emulates the instruction, writes the result to the trapped register image or to user memory, and advances the trapped instruction pointer on success.
Emulation uses a ten byte result buffer sufficient for the largest table store result.
A frame header occupies two machine words.
Alternative stack realignment allowances exist for different build configurations, with values of three and one words.

Frame based unwinding refuses user mode registers, repairs a null instruction pointer case by synthesizing a frame from the stack pointer, initializes stack tracking, then advances to the requested starting frame.
Guess based unwinding aligns the starting frame, initializes stack tracking, and advances once when the start is off stack or does not point at kernel text.
Object based unwinding keeps post init read only flags for initialization, debugging and lookup sizing, with debugging enabled through an early command line switch.
Unstable timekeeping aborts refinement and retires the early source without promoting the full source, while observed backward steps across processors can permanently disable the time stamp clock.
Starting unwind from user mode yields an unknown stack type with no further progress, and the null instruction pointer repair must preserve the original frame pointer for later steps.
